messages.subject: stat_bin2d with geom_text
parts:
Hi,

I have a question that is related to Rob's: (see below)

How can I use geoms other than "rect" with stat_bin2d?

I have tried

stat_bin2d(geom="text", aes(x=x, y=y, label=..count..), bins=3)

but it doesn't work.

Reproducible code:

df <- data.frame(v1=runif(2000), v2=runif(2000))
pl <- ggplot(df) + xlim(c(0,1)) + ylim(c(0,1))

# This works of course:
pl + stat_bin2d(geom="rect", aes(x=v1, y=v2, fill=..count..), bins=3)


# But:
pl + stat_bin2d(geom="text", aes(x=v1, y=v2, label=..count..), bins=3)

# gives the Error: geom_text requires the following missing aesthetics: x, y

pl + stat_bin2d(geom="point", aes(x=v1, y=v2, size=..count..), bins=3)
# Error: geom_point requires the following missing aesthetics: x, y

pl + stat_bin2d(geom="text", aes(x=..xmax.., y=..ymax.., label=..count..), bins=3)

# Runs without error, but draws nothing.

What am I getting wrong here?

The idea behind this is to create a colour coded kind of "confusion matrix" reprsenting the correlation between two biological assays with continuous readouts between 0 and 1.  

Thanks for any help,

Sebastian

On Wed, May 19, 2010 at 8:48 AM, <sebastia...@basf.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I have a question that is related to Rob's: (see below)
>
> How can I use geoms other than "rect" with stat_bin2d?
>
> I have tried
>
> stat_bin2d(geom="text", aes(x=x, y=y, label=..count..), bins=3)
>
> but it doesn't work.
>
> Reproducible code:
>
> df <- data.frame(v1=runif(2000), v2=runif(2000))
> pl <- ggplot(df) + xlim(c(0,1)) + ylim(c(0,1))
>
> # This works of course:
> pl + stat_bin2d(geom="rect", aes(x=v1, y=v2, fill=..count..), bins=3)
>
>
> # But:
> pl + stat_bin2d(geom="text", aes(x=v1, y=v2, label=..count..), bins=3)
>
> # gives the Error: geom_text requires the following missing aesthetics: x, y

You get this error because stat_bin2d is optimised to work with
geom_rect - it returns xmin, xmax, ymin and ymax aesthetics, not the x
and y aesthetics that geom_text needs. There's no simple alternative
except to do the summarisation yourself.

Hadley
